title: 'Observability' Was Coined for Control Systems, Not Software
explainer: The term observability didn't start in software at all: engineer Rudolf Kalman introduced it in a 1960 control-theory paper to describe whether a system's internal state can be fully reconstructed just from watching its external outputs, formalized with a linear-algebra rank condition on what's now called the observability matrix. Modern software observability borrows that exact idea - logs, metrics, and traces are the 'external outputs' engineers use to infer the internal state of a distributed system they cannot directly inspect, decades after Kalman defined the underlying mathematics for very different machines.

resources.title: From Kalman to Kubernetes: A History of Observability in IT
